**Yes**, the standard deduction is available to salaried employees under Section 16(ia) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, for the Financial Year 2024-25. However, the amount of this deduction varies depending on whether the taxpayer opts for the Old or New Tax Regime.

### Legal Analysis and Provisions

**1. General Availability and Old Regime**
The standard deduction is a statutory deduction allowed from gross salary income before computing the income under the head “Salaries” [C3]. For taxpayers opting for the **Old Tax Regime**, the standard deduction under Section 16(ia) is available as per the provisions contained in the Income-tax Act [C1]. The specific amount for the Old Regime is not explicitly detailed in the provided context chunks, but it is a standard component of salary deductions alongside Entertainment Allowance and Professional Tax [C5].

**2. New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC)**
For taxpayers opting for the **New Tax Regime** under Section 115BAC, the standard deduction is available but subject to a specific cap:
*   An employee can claim the standard deduction under Section 16(ia) only to the extent of **Rs. 75,000** [C2].
*   This cap applies specifically to the New Tax Regime as per the validation rules and statutory interpretations provided [C2].

**3. Distinction from Other Deductions**
It is important to distinguish the standard deduction from other salary deductions which are **not** available under the New Tax Regime:
*   **Entertainment Allowance (Section 16(ii)):** Cannot be claimed if the New Tax Regime is selected [C7]. It is available only if the Old Tax Regime is opted for [C4].
*   **Professional Tax (Section 16(iii)):** Cannot be claimed if the New Tax Regime is selected [C7].

**4. Reporting in Income Tax Return (ITR)**
*   The standard deduction admissible under Section 16(ia) should be entered in the ITR as per Part B of Form 16 [C5].
*   In the context of Form 16, the standard deduction is listed as a deduction under Section 16 [C1].

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Old Regime** | Available | As per statutory provisions (not specified in context) [C1] |
| **New Regime (Sec 115BAC)** | Available | Capped at **Rs. 75,000** [C2] |
